assembly_notes: The root is always the folded C-frame: one bored screw station per clamp_form candidate, an upright post, a post lock knob, a height carriage on a prismatic stroke and its own lock knob. The carriage adapts its shoulder locally: swing families get a vertical spigot, the vertical-plane parallelogram gets a bored clevis plus a strut bracket. Every arm candidate publishes one vertical head seat and every tray_head candidate consumes it with a yaw collar, so the deck stays level regardless of the arm family. All revolute and continuous joints are solved with mate_axes and registered with register_interface_mate; pin joints use bored fork cheeks with a connecting web, and sliding members run in real bores or channels. No ctx.allow_overlap is used anywhere. The desk clamp now also offers an over-centre cam station: a frame-mounted cam lever drives a prismatic follower jaw that carries the same pressure shoe on the same clamping axis, so the throat closes identically for either actuation. The tray head gains a rear fold hinge whose deck is offset forward of the pin so parking swings it up and back. Two orthogonal head slots ride on every tray candidate: the width interface (a plain deck or two captured side rails on bounded strokes) and the tilt lock (a friction knob or a toothed sector plus a pawl part on the tray).
